sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:9

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:9:1
items.html:
One Parsa in the middle of his Guf … and draws from above and gives to below: Parsa means the concluding screen of the Partzuf, similar to the toes of the feet, which are the conclusion of the Partzuf. The difference between them, however, is in the terms of internality and externality: the Parsa is the discernment of the Sium of the inner Partzufim, whereas the toes of the feet are the discernment of the Sium of the externality of the Partzuf as well. And this Parsa was made (16) after the upper coupling that was made in the Nikvey Einayim, which means that the place of the coupling was raised from the place of the Peh [mouth], which is the Malchut of the Rosh [head], to the place of the Nikvey Einayim, which is the Hochma of the Rosh, as above at length (on page 391, the passage beginning “The hairs”). And then the ten Sefirot of the Rosh were divided into two degrees, Rosh and Guf [body], and the distance between them is great; for in the Rosh there are as yet no vessels and no actual discernment of clothing, since the reflected light there operates in the manner of below upward, and not in the manner of above downward, which is what clothing means. Rather, the Malchut of the Rosh, by the force of the coupling made in the screen in her, expands into ten Sefirot of her own and within her, and then the light clothes in her from above downward, that is, in complete clothing. Now that the place of the screen and the coupling has been raised to the Nikvey Einayim, which is the Hochma of the Rosh, and the reflected light rises and clothes the direct light from Hochma upward to Keter, it turns out that the Malchut in that Hochma afterwards expands and spreads with the direct light in her from above downward, that is, to the three Sefirot, Bina and ZON of the Rosh. And these Bina, ZA, and Malchut, which are called AHP, became discernments of Sefirot of a Guf, meaning vessels of reception for that light which emerges from the coupling in the Nikvey Einayim. Thus there was made here, out of the ten Sefirot of a single Rosh, a complete Partzuf of Rosh and Guf, in which the Galgalta and Einayim alone remained as the discernment of a Rosh, while the Ozen [ear], Hotem [nose], and Peh that were in it became the discernment of a Guf for that Rosh.
Now, in the same measure by which the root Malchut of the Rosh was raised from the Peh to the Nikvey Einayim, so were the ten Sefirot of the Sium of that Partzuf SAG divided. For the ten Sefirot that conclude the Partzuf begin in SAG (16) from the place of the Chazeh until the Sium of the feet: the discernment of Keter and Hochma in it expands from the place of the Chazeh to the Tabur, and the three Sefirot, Bina, ZA, and Malchut in it, expand from the Tabur to the Sium of the feet. It turns out now that, just as the Bina, ZA, and Malchut of the Rosh went outside the discernment of the Rosh and became the discernment of a Guf, so the Bina, ZA, and Malchut of the Sefirot of the Sium went out entirely from the discernment of the emanation of the Partzuf. Thus that screen which concludes the Partzuf, which had stood in the Malchut of the ten Sefirot of the Sium — which is the place of the toes of the feet — has now risen to the Hochma of these ten Sefirot, which is the place of the Tabur; and the three Sefirot, Bina, ZA, and Malchut, which are below the Tabur, went out entirely from the Partzuf, and the discernment of the emanation of that Partzuf was annulled in them. By this you will well understand that those nine lower Sefirot of SAG, which formerly expanded from the Tabur to the Sium of the feet of the inner AK, and which rose as MAN to the Taamim of SAG and to the discernment of the Nikvey Einayim, did not return and descend afterwards to their original place, that is, down to the Sium of the feet of AK. For the place of the point of the Sium of the Partzuf SAG had already changed, being now at the place of the Tabur, and the screen that concludes SAG had already been spread there, as above. Rather, they remained above the Tabur and the Parsa, and only the ZON of the inner AK, which had been included with them, descended by themselves below the Tabur. And the matter of “and draws from above and gives to below,” as well as the matter of the breaking through, that the light broke through the Parsa, will be explained further on.
